name: IBM PC 5150 with Intel 8087 coprocessor
notes: Peak FMUL rate 0.034-0.055 million/s for an 8087 at 5 MHz (x87 timing table); IBM PC ran the 8087 at 4.77 MHz, so ~5% lower. Coprocessor socket in IBM PC per Intel_8087 article.

name: Intel 80387 (16 MHz) with 80386
notes: Peak FMUL rate 0.280-0.552 million/s at 16 MHz (x87 timing table); 33 MHz parts later reached 1.1 million/s. Released 1987.

name: Intel 486DX-50
notes: Peak FMUL rate 1.0-3.1 million/s at 50 MHz (x87 timing table); 50 MHz i486DX introduced fall 1991 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I486). The FLOPS article's per-cycle table gives 0.128 FLOP/cycle, i.e. 6.4 MFLOPS at 50 MHz.

name: Intel Pentium 60 MHz
notes: 0.5 FLOP/cycle/core (FLOPS article table) x 60 MHz. The x87 timing table instead gives 20-60 million FMUL/s at 60 MHz.

name: Intel Pentium III 1.0 GHz (Coppermine)
notes: 2 FP32 FLOP/cycle (FLOPS article) x 1000 MHz; 1 GHz part released between Dec 1999 and May 2000 per Pentium III article.

name: Intel Pentium 4 3.06 GHz (Northwood)
notes: 4 FP32 FLOP/cycle (FLOPS article) x 3.06 GHz; released Nov 2002. FP64 would be half.

name: Intel Core 2 Extreme X6800
notes: 8 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 2 cores x 2.93 GHz; released July 29, 2006. FP64 half.

name: Intel Core i7-920 (Bloomfield)
notes: 8 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 4 cores x 2.66 GHz base; released 2008-11-17.

name: Intel Core i7-2600K (Sandy Bridge)
notes: 16 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 4 cores x 3.4 GHz base (3.8 GHz turbo); released 2011-01-09.

name: Intel Core i7-4770K (Haswell)
notes: 32 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 4 cores x 3.5 GHz base (3.9 GHz turbo); released 2013-06-02.

name: Intel Core i9-9900K (Coffee Lake Refresh)
notes: 32 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 8 cores x 3.6 GHz base (all-core turbo 4.7 GHz would give ~1.2 TFLOPS); announced Oct 2018.

name: AMD Ryzen 9 3950X (Zen 2)
notes: 32 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 16 cores x 3.5 GHz base (4.7 GHz boost); released 2019-11-25.

name: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X (Zen 5)
notes: 64 FP32 FLOP/cycle/core x 16 cores x 4.3 GHz base (5.7 GHz boost); released 2024-08-15.

name: Nvidia GeForce 8800 GTX
notes: First unified-shader GeForce. 128 shaders x 1350 MHz x 2 (MAD). Wikipedia also lists 518.4 GFLOPS counting the extra co-issued MUL (3 ops/clock); MAD-only figure used for consistency.

name: ATI Radeon HD 2900 XT
notes: 320 stream processors x 743 MHz x 2 (MAD). Released May 14, 2007.

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 280
notes: 240 shaders x 1296 MHz x 2 (MAD); the co-issued MUL is not counted (marketing figures that include it are ~1.5x higher).

name: ATI Radeon HD 4870
notes: 800 stream processors x 750 MHz x 2 (MAD). One of the first consumer GPUs to reach 1 TFLOPS (FLOPS article).

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 480
notes: 480 shaders x 1401 MHz x 2 (FMA).

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 580
notes: 512 shaders x 1544 MHz x 2 (FMA).

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 680
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity; 3090.4 GFLOPS at base clock.

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 780 Ti
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity; 5040 GFLOPS at base clock.

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 980 Ti
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity; 5632 GFLOPS at base clock.

name: Nvidia GeForce GTX 1080 Ti
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity; 10616 GFLOPS at base clock.

name: Nvidia GeForce RTX 2080 Ti
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity (reference 1545 MHz boost; Founders Edition was clocked slightly higher); tensor-core FP16 figures not used.

name: Nvidia GeForce RTX 3090
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity. Ampere doubled FP32 lanes per SM (10496 CUDA cores), so this peak is harder to reach in practice than on earlier architectures.

name: Nvidia GeForce RTX 4090
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity. Also listed in the FLOPS article as 82.6 TFLOPS.

name: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090
notes: FP32 FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, at reference boost clock (Wikipedia table cites TechPowerUp GPU DB); no sparsity; 87.78 TFLOPS at base clock. Released Jan 30, 2025.

name: Nintendo 64
notes: CPU (NEC VR4300 at 93.75 MHz) figure from the former 'Nintendo 64 technical specifications' Wikipedia article, citing a MIPS Technologies product card; = 1 FLOP/cycle. RCP graphics coprocessor not counted.

name: Sega Dreamcast
notes: Hitachi SH-4 CPU at 200 MHz with 128-bit graphics-oriented FPU; PowerVR2 GPU is fixed-function and not counted. JP release Nov 27, 1998.

name: Sony PlayStation 2
notes: Emotion Engine CPU at ~295 MHz; GPU (Graphics Synthesizer) fixed-function, not counted. JP release March 4, 2000.

name: Nintendo GameCube
notes: Gekko CPU at 486 MHz. The GameCube article also quotes a 'peak of 10.5 GFLOPS' for the whole system, which is not used here.

name: Microsoft Xbox
notes: NV2A GPU at 233 MHz, single-precision figure from Wikipedia's console-GPU table. Uncertain: other figures circulate (4.66, 5.8, 20 GFLOPS). The 733 MHz Pentium III CPU adds ~1.5 GFLOPS (2 FLOP/cycle SSE).

name: Microsoft Xbox 360
notes: ATI Xenos GPU at 500 MHz (48 unified vec5 shaders x MAD). The Xenon CPU adds a theoretical 115.2 GFLOPS (Xbox 360 technical specifications article), not included. Released Nov 22, 2005.

name: Sony PlayStation 3
notes: RSX GPU only. Wikipedia's Nvidia console-GPU table gives 192 + 153.6 GFLOPS with the Cell SPUs; Sony's launch-era '2 TFLOPS' claim is not used. Released Nov 11, 2006.

name: Nintendo Wii
notes: Broadway CPU at 729 MHz; Hollywood GPU is fixed-function, not counted.

name: Sony PlayStation 4
notes: 18 GCN compute units at 800 MHz. Released Nov 15, 2013.

name: Microsoft Xbox One
notes: 12 GCN compute units (768 cores) at 853 MHz. Released Nov 22, 2013.

name: Sony PlayStation 4 Pro
notes: 36 CUs at 911 MHz; often rounded to 4.2 TFLOPS. FP16 rate is double, not used.

name: Microsoft Xbox One X
notes: 40 CUs at 1172 MHz (= 6.0 TFLOPS). Released Nov 7, 2017.

name: Nintendo Switch
notes: Tegra X1 GPU, 256 CUDA cores x 2 x 768 MHz docked; 236 GFLOPS undocked at 460 MHz.

name: Sony PlayStation 5
notes: 36 RDNA 2 CUs at up to 2.23 GHz (variable clock). FLOPS article: 20.56 TFLOPS at FP16, not used.

name: Microsoft Xbox Series X
notes: 52 RDNA 2 CUs at a fixed 1.825 GHz. Released Nov 10, 2020.

name: Nintendo Switch 2
notes: 1536 Ampere CUDA cores at 1007 MHz docked; 1.71 TFLOPS undocked. Released June 5, 2025.
